text: The device hums. Green hills, a stone sheepfold, and a boy with a staff waving you over.

speaker: David
text: Shalom! I am David. Three of my sheep have wandered off. Help me bring them back to the fold?

speaker: David
text: They cannot have gone far, {name}.

speaker: Keeper
text: That boy never loses a sheep. Not one.
The sheep trots after you.
The gate of the sheepfold.
No strays with you yet.
Safe inside!

speaker: David
text: All here! Listen. Something is happening in town, but I cannot leave the flock. Go and see!
The sheep come first. David is counting on you.

speaker: Elder
text: Do you come in peace?

speaker: Samuel
text: In peace, | I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.
Samuel was God's prophet, and God had sent him to choose Israel's next king while King Saul was still on the throne. No wonder the elders were nervous.

speaker: Elder
text: A prophet does not visit a small town for nothing.
Samuel stands by the altar, waiting.

speaker: Jesse
text: The prophet has invited my family to the sacrifice! {name}, would you call my sons? Seven of them are around the town.
He is busy and barely looks up.
He stands very still, waiting his turn.
Eliab, the firstborn, splits a log with one swing. He towers over you. He nods and goes.
Abinadab hauls up a full bucket as if it weighed nothing. He nods and goes.
Shammah has broad shoulders and a quick smile. He dusts off his hands and goes.
Nethanel carries two full jars without spilling a drop. He sets them down and goes.
Raddai is across the field before you finish speaking. He must be the fastest.
Ozem asks three sharp questions about the prophet, then goes. He seems clever.
The seventh brother wakes with a start under the tree and hurries off, still yawning.
You chose {pick}. He certainly looks the part.
Not {pick}.

speaker: Samuel
text: Surely here before the LORD is His anointed.

speaker: The LORD
text: Do not consider his appearance or height, for I have rejected him; the LORD does not see as man does.

speaker: The LORD
text: For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.
Samuel judged Eliab by how he looked. You probably judged by looks too! God looks deeper, at what a person loves, trusts and wants.

speaker: Samuel
text: The LORD has not chosen this one either.

speaker: Samuel
text: The LORD has not chosen any of these.

speaker: Samuel
text: Are these all the sons you have?

speaker: Jesse
text: There is still the youngest, | but he is tending the sheep.

speaker: Samuel
text: Send for him, | For we will not sit down to eat until he arrives.

speaker: Jesse
text: {name}! You know the pasture. Run!

speaker: David
text: The prophet is asking for me? Keeper, watch the flock!

speaker: The LORD
text: Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.
So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward.
God chose the youngest son, the one left out in the fields. God often uses the people everyone else overlooks.
Long after, another King from David's family was born here in Bethlehem. An angel told shepherds in the fields nearby:

speaker: An angel
text: Today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you. He is Christ the Lord!
Christ means "the Anointed One." Like David, Jesus was God's chosen King.
Then Samuel set out and went to Ramah.

speaker: David
text: I should get back to the sheep.
Your device buzzes. Time to go.

speaker: Townsman
text: Fresh bread and roast meat. I can hardly wait.

speaker: Townsman
text: Nobody sits until the boy arrives? Then run faster!
Deep scratches in the rock. Claws. Years later, David will tell King Saul about days like that:

speaker: David
text: … whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock, I went after it, struck it down, and delivered the lamb from its mouth.
A small harp, resting on a rock. David wrote songs. One of them begins like this:
The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside quiet waters.

speaker: The LORD
text: Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.

speaker: The LORD
text: Take a heifer with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’

speaker: Jesse
text: Seven sons here. And the youngest is out with the sheep.
Now David was the son of a man named Jesse, an Ephrathite from Bethlehem of Judah who had eight sons.

speaker: Neighbor
text: A king should look like a king. Have you ever seen King Saul?
… a head taller than any of the people.
Years from now, far from home, David will remember this well:

speaker: David
text: Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!
Long ago, a woman named Ruth gathered grain in these fields. Her baby grew up to be Jesse's father.
… they named him Obed. He became the father of Jesse, the father of David.

Bethlehem means House of Bread.
